claim: Recent studies of the Central Complex in the brain of the fruit fly have identified neurons with activity that tracks the animal's heading direction.
source: Recent studies of the Central Complex in the brain of the fruit fly have identified neurons with activity that tracks the animal's heading direction.
evidence: This is a statement about recent research findings on fruit fly neurons in the Central Complex.

claim: Neurons in the Central Complex are part of a neuronal circuit with dynamics resembling those of a ring attractor.
source: These neurons are part of a neuronal circuit with dynamics resembling those of a ring attractor.
evidence: This describes the circuit dynamics based on research findings.

claim: The homologous circuit in other insects has similar topographic structure but with significant structural and connectivity differences.
source: The homologous circuit in other insects has similar topographic structure but with significant structural and connectivity differences.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about circuit structure across species.

claim: The circuit found in locusts can operate as a ring attractor.
source: We illustrate that the circuit found in locusts can also operate as a ring attractor
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling work presented in the manuscript.

claim: Differences in the inhibition pattern enable the fruit fly circuit to respond faster to heading changes.
source: differences in the inhibition pattern enable the fruit fly circuit to respond faster to heading changes
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the two circuit models.

claim: Additional recurrent connections render the locust circuit more tolerant to noise.
source: additional recurrent connections render the locust circuit more tolerant to noise
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling and analysis of circuit properties.

claim: Subtle differences in neuronal projection patterns can have a significant effect on circuit performance.
source: Our findings demonstrate that subtle differences in neuronal projection patterns can have a significant effect on circuit performance
evidence: This is a general conclusion drawn from the comparative analysis.

claim: A neuronal circuit with activity that tracks heading direction provides a potential basis for an internal compass mechanism in insects.
source: In insects, the discovery of a neuronal circuit with activity that tracks heading direction provides a potential basis for an internal compass mechanism (Zhang, 1996; Homberg, 2004; Heinze and Reppert, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: An internal compass can mediate maintaining a straight course.
source: Such an internal compass can mediate a simple navigation competence such as maintaining a straight course (Dacke et al., 2003; Mouritsen and Frost, 2002)
evidence: This is supported by citations to behavioral studies.

claim: An internal compass can mediate reorienting to a target after distractions.
source: or reorienting to a target after distractions (Neuser et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a behavioral study.

claim: An internal compass is essential for path integration which enables central-place foragers to return directly to their nest after long and convoluted outward paths.
source: but is also essential for the more complex navigational process of path integration (or dead reckoning) which enables central-place foragers to return directly to their nest after long and convoluted outward paths (Darwin, 1873; von Frisch, 1967; Mittelstaedt and Mittelstaedt, 1980; Müller and Wehner, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to classic navigation studies.

claim: The central complex (CX) is implicated in many navigation-related processes.
source: a brain region called the central complex (CX) is implicated in many navigation-related processes.
evidence: This is a general statement about the role of the CX based on existing literature.

claim: The CX of the insect brain is an unpaired, midline-spanning set of neuropils that consist of the protocerebral bridge (PB), the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body and the paired noduli.
source: The CX of the insect brain is an unpaired, midline-spanning set of neuropils that consist of the protocerebral bridge (PB), the ellipsoid body (also called lower division of the central body), the fan-shaped body (also called upper division of the central body) and the paired noduli.
evidence: This is an anatomical description based on established knowledge.

claim: The neuropils and their characteristic internal organisation in vertical slices combined with horizontal layers are highly conserved across insect species.
source: These neuropils and their characteristic internal organisation in vertical slices combined with horizontal layers are highly conserved across insect species.
evidence: This is a comparative anatomical statement based on existing knowledge.

claim: The structured projection patterns of columnar cells result in the PB being organised in 16 or 18 contiguous glomeruli and the ellipsoid body (EB) in eight adjoined tiles.
source: The structured projection patterns of columnar cells result in the PB being organised in 16 or 18 contiguous glomeruli and the ellipsoid body (EB) in eight adjoined tiles.
evidence: This is an anatomical description based on established knowledge.

claim: The CX is of key importance for the computations required to derive a heading signal.
source: Crucially, the CX is of key importance for the computations required to derive a heading signal (Pfeiffer and Homberg, 2014; Triphan et al., 2010; Neuser et al., 2008; Ofstad et al., 2011; Homberg, 2004; Homberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: In locusts, intracellular recordings have revealed a neuronal layout that topographically maps the animal's orientation relative to simulated skylight cues, including polarised light and point sources of light.
source: In locusts (Schistocerca gregaria), intracellular recordings have revealed a neuronal layout that topographically maps the animal's orientation relative to simulated skylight cues, including polarised light and point sources of light (Heinze and Homberg, 2007; el Jundi et al., 2014; Pegel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to electrophysiological studies in locusts.

claim: Calcium imaging of columnar neurons connecting the EB and the PB (E-PG neurons) in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster revealed that the E-PG neuronal ensemble maintains localised spiking activity that moves from one group of neurons to the next as the animal rotates with respect to its surrounding.
source: Calcium imaging of columnar neurons connecting the EB and the PB (E-PG neurons) in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster revealed that the E-PG neuronal ensemble maintains localised spiking activity — commonly called an activity 'bump' — that moves from one group of neurons to the next as the animal rotates with respect to its surrounding (Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015; Giraldo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to calcium imaging studies.

claim: The heading signal is maintained in restrained flies walking on an air-supported rotating ball.
source: This has been confirmed for restrained flies walking on an air-supported rotating ball (Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: The heading signal is maintained in tethered flies flying in a virtual reality environment.
source: as well as tethered flies flying in a virtual reality environment (Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: The heading signal is maintained even when the visual stimulus is removed, and it moves relative to the (no longer visible) cue as the animal walks in darkness.
source: Notably, the heading signal (the activity 'bump') is maintained even when the visual stimulus is removed, and it moves relative to the (no longer visible) cue as the animal walks in darkness (Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: The underlying circuit combines idiothetic and allothetic information into a coherent heading signal.
source: The underlying circuit therefore combines idiothetic and allothetic information into a coherent heading signal.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations cited.

claim: The neuronal activity in the insect CX appears to constitute an internal encoding of heading which closely resembles the hypothetical ring attractor proposed by Skaggs et al., 1995 to account for the rat 'head direction' cells.
source: Overall, this neuronal activity appears to constitute an internal encoding of heading in the insect's CX, which closely resembles the hypothetical ring attractor (Amari, 1977) proposed by Skaggs et al., 1995 to account for the rat 'head direction' cells (Taube et al., 1990; Blair and Sharp, 1995; Redish et al., 1996; Stackman and Taube, 1998; Goodridge et al., 1998; Goodridge and Touretzky, 2000; Sharp et al., 2001; Taube and Bassett, 2003; Stratton et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to theoretical and experimental work on ring attractors and head direction cells.

claim: Input to the ring attractor circuit results in a single localised 'bump' of activity centred in one subset of the neurons while other neuronal units are silenced.
source: input to the circuit results in a single localised 'bump' of activity — centred in one subset of the neurons — while other neuronal units are silenced
evidence: This describes a key property of ring attractors based on theoretical models.

claim: The activity 'bump' can move around the attractor space, which forms a ring, in a manner that consistently tracks some property of the input.
source: the activity 'bump' can move around the attractor space, which forms a ring, in a manner that consistently tracks some property of the input
evidence: This describes a key property of ring attractors based on theoretical models.

claim: The 'bump' of activity is maintained for some time after all input is removed.
source: and the 'bump' of activity is maintained for some time after all input is removed.
evidence: This describes a key property of ring attractors based on theoretical models.

claim: Ring attractor properties can be obtained by utilising opposing excitatory and inhibitory connections with excitatory lateral connections to neighbouring neuronal units and inhibitory ones affecting neurons on the opposite side of the ring.
source: These properties can be obtained, in computational neural models, by utilising opposing excitatory and inhibitory connections with excitatory lateral connections to neighbouring neuronal units and inhibitory ones affecting neurons on the opposite side of the ring.
evidence: This describes the computational mechanism underlying ring attractors.

claim: Cope et al., 2017 proposed a ring attractor model that is inspired by the rat 'head direction' cell model of Skaggs et al., 1995.
source: Cope et al., 2017 proposed a ring attractor model that is inspired by the rat 'head direction' cell model of Skaggs et al., 1995.
evidence: This is a citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: Kakaria and de Bivort, 2017 presented a spiking neuronal model consisting of the four types of CX neurons shown to play a role in heading encoding: E-PG, P-EN, P-EG, and Delta7 neurons.
source: Kakaria and de Bivort, 2017 presented a spiking neuronal model consisting of the four types of CX neurons shown to play a role in heading encoding: E-PG, P-EN, P-EG, and Delta7 neurons.
evidence: This is a citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: The model by Kakaria and de Bivort, 2017 demonstrated that the neuron set E-PG, P-EN, P-EG, and Delta7 is sufficient for exhibiting ring attractor behaviour.
source: Their model demonstrated that this neuron set is sufficient for exhibiting ring attractor behaviour.
evidence: This is a finding from a previous modeling study.

claim: Su et al., 2017 implemented a spiking neuronal model consisting of the E-PG, P-EN, and P-EG neurons with inhibition provided by a group of R ring neurons.
source: In contrast, Su et al., 2017 implemented a spiking neuronal model consisting of the E-PG, P-EN, and P-EG neurons with inhibition provided by a group of R ring neurons.
evidence: This is a citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: The key neurons variously involved in the hypothetical ring attractor circuit are the E-PG, P-EN, P-EG, Delta7 and R ring neurons.
source: In both neurobiological studies and computational models, the key neurons variously involved in the hypothetical ring attractor circuit are the E-PG, P-EN, P-EG, Delta7 and R ring neurons (Wolff and Rubin, 2018; Wolff et al., 2015; Kakaria and de Bivort, 2017; Su et al., 2017; Green et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The E-PG, P-EN and P-EG neurons have been postulated to be excitatory while Delta7 or R ring neurons are conjectured to be mediating the inhibition.
source: The E-PG, P-EN and P-EG neurons have been postulated to be excitatory while Delta7 or R ring neurons are conjectured to be mediating the inhibition (Kakaria and de Bivort, 2017; Su et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to modeling studies.

claim: The E-PG and P-EN neurons are postulated to form synapses in the PB and in the EB forming a recurrent circuit.
source: The E-PG and P-EN neurons are postulated to form synapses in the PB and in the EB forming a recurrent circuit.
evidence: This is a statement about circuit connectivity based on existing models.

claim: The ring attractor state is set by a mapping of the azimuthal position of visual cues to E-PG neurons around the ring which are assumed to receive the positional input to this circuit.
source: The ring attractor state is set by a mapping of the azimuthal position of visual cues to E-PG neurons around the ring which are assumed to receive the positional input to this circuit.
evidence: This describes how the ring attractor is initialized based on existing models.

claim: P-EN neurons shift the heading signal around the ring attractor when stimulated, in a fashion similar to the left-right rotation neurons proposed by Skaggs et al., 1995.
source: Furthermore, P-EN neurons shift the heading signal around the ring attractor when stimulated, in a fashion similar to the left-right rotation neurons proposed by Skaggs et al., 1995 (Turner-Evans et al., 2017; Green et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental and theoretical studies.

claim: Two main types of ring attractor implementation exist: one with local excitation and global, uniform, inhibition and another one characterised by sinusoidally modulated inhibition across the ring attractor.
source: In principle, two main types of ring attractor implementation exist: one with local excitation and global, uniform, inhibition and another one characterised by sinusoidally modulated inhibition across the ring attractor.
evidence: This is a statement about theoretical ring attractor models.

claim: Kim et al., 2017 concluded that the observed dynamics of E-PG neurons can best be modelled using a ring attractor with local excitation and uniform global inhibition.
source: Kim et al., 2017 have experimentally explored the type of ring attractor that could underlie the head direction circuit of the fruit fly and concluded that the observed dynamics of E-PG neurons can best be modelled using a ring attractor with local excitation and uniform global inhibition.
evidence: This is a citation to an experimental study.

claim: The CX is highly conserved on a broad level, but details at the level of single neurons vary between insect species.
source: Although the CX is highly conserved on a broad level, details at the level of single neurons vary between insect species.
evidence: This is a comparative anatomical statement based on existing knowledge.

claim: The EB of the locust is not closed around the edges, but is crescent-shaped, preventing the E-PG neurons from forming a physical ring.
source: First, as in most insects except Drosophila, the EB of the locust is not closed around the edges, but is crescent-shaped, preventing the E-PG neurons from forming a physical ring.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation comparing the two species, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: The Drosophila PB consists of nine glomeruli per hemisphere, and accordingly 18 groups of E-PG neurons.
source: Second, the Drosophila PB consists of nine glomeruli per hemisphere, and accordingly 18 groups of E-PG neurons.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation about Drosophila, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: In locusts, there are 8 glomeruli per hemisphere and 16 groups of neurons.
source: In locusts, there are 8 glomeruli per hemisphere and 16 groups of neurons.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation about locusts, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: Delta7 neurons (TB1 neurons in the locust) possess two columnar output sites located eight glomeruli apart in all species.
source: Whereas these cells possess two columnar output sites located eight glomeruli apart in all species
evidence: This is a comparative anatomical statement.

claim: Delta7 neurons have an approximately uniform density across the PB glomeruli in Drosophila.
source: their dendrites have an approximately uniform density across the PB glomeruli in Drosophila.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation about Drosophila, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: In the desert locust, the postsynaptic domains of the eight Delta7 neurons are restricted to particular glomeruli of the PB, avoiding the regions around the output branches.
source: This differs substantially from the dendritic distribution in the desert locust, in which the postsynaptic domains of the eight Delta7 neurons are restricted to particular glomeruli of the PB, avoiding the regions around the output branches.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation about locusts, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: The Delta7 dendritic pattern in locusts is conserved in other species such as the Monarch butterfly, the sweat bee, and two species of dung beetles.
source: This pattern is conserved in other species as well, such as in the Monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus), the sweat bee (Megalopta genalis), as well as in two species of dung beetles (Scarabaeus lamarcki and Scarabaeus satyrus) (Heinze and Homberg, 2007; Heinze et al., 2013; Stone et al., 2017; El Jundi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to comparative anatomical studies.

claim: Each Delta7 neuron has presynaptic terminal domains in two or three glomeruli along the PB in both species.
source: Study of the actual neuronal anatomy of Delta7 neurons in the PB shows that, in both species, each Delta7 neuron has presynaptic terminal domains in two or three glomeruli along the PB (Heinze and Homberg, 2007; Wolff and Rubin, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The presynaptic terminal domains of Delta7 neurons are separated by seven glomeruli.
source: These presynaptic terminal domains are separated by seven glomeruli (Figure 2A and Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In Drosophila, the Delta7 neurons have postsynaptic terminals across all remaining glomeruli of the PB.
source: In Drosophila, the Delta7 neurons have postsynaptic terminals across all remaining glomeruli of the PB (Wolff and Rubin, 2018; Franconville et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies.

claim: In locusts the Delta7 neurons have postsynaptic terminal domains only in specific glomeruli.
source: while in locusts the Delta7 neurons have postsynaptic terminal domains only in specific glomeruli (Heinze and Homberg, 2007; Beetz et al., 2015; Hadeln et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies.

claim: There are eight types of Delta7 neurons in the PB, each having the same pattern of synaptic terminals shifted by one glomerulus.
source: There are eight types of Delta7 neurons in the PB, each having the same pattern of synaptic terminals shifted by one glomerulus (Figure 2A and Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: In fruit flies each Delta7 neuron forms synapses and inhibits all other Delta7 neurons.
source: That is, in fruit flies each Delta7 neuron forms synapses and inhibits all other Delta7 neurons.
evidence: This is derived from the connectivity analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the locust each Delta7 neuron only inhibits a subset of Delta7 neurons with weakening synaptic strengths towards its nearest neighbours.
source: In contrast, in the locust each Delta7 neuron only inhibits a subset of Delta7 neurons with weakening synaptic strengths towards its nearest neighbours (Heinze and Homberg, 2007).
evidence: This is derived from the connectivity analysis shown in Figure 2 and supported by a citation.

claim: The effective global inhibition pattern found in the fruit fly fits the observation of Kim et al., 2017 that calcium dynamics better matched a ring attractor with global inhibition in this species.
source: The effective global inhibition pattern found in the fruit fly fits the observation of Kim et al., 2017 that calcium dynamics better matched a ring attractor with global inhibition in this species.
evidence: This connects the modeling results to experimental observations.

claim: The effective circuits of the locust and the fruit fly are equivalent in their effective structure, forming a closed ring attractor in both species with an identical functional role for each neuron class.
source: The similarity between the effective circuits of the locust and the fruit fly is striking. Despite the fact that locusts have eight PB glomeruli while fruit flies have nine, both circuits form closed rings organised in eight octants with the functional role of each neuron class appearing to be identical.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: The E-PG neurons were presynaptic to both P-EG and P-EN neurons, with P-EG neurons forming recurrent synapses back to E-PG neurons.
source: The E-PG neurons were presynaptic to both P-EG and P-EN neurons, with P-EG neurons forming recurrent synapses back to E-PG neurons.
evidence: This describes the connectivity pattern derived from the circuit analysis.

claim: P-EN neurons were presynaptic to E-PG neurons with a shift of one octant to the left or right.
source: P-EN neurons were presynaptic to E-PG neurons with a shift of one octant to the left or right.
evidence: This describes the connectivity pattern derived from the circuit analysis.

claim: Two of the main anatomical differences between the two species (eight versus nine PB glomeruli and ring-shaped versus crescent-shaped EB) had no fundamental effect on the principal structure of the CX heading direction circuit.
source: Overall, two of the main anatomical differences between the two species (eight versus nine PB glomeruli and ring-shaped versus crescent-shaped EB) had no fundamental effect on the principal structure of the CX heading direction circuit.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparative circuit analysis.

claim: The order of E-PG neuronal projections in the EB differs between the two species.
source: During our analysis of the anatomical data in locusts and flies, we observed that the order of E-PG neuronal projections in the EB differs between the two species (Heinze and Homberg, 2008; Williams, 1975; Wolff et al., 2015; Wolff and Rubin, 2018).
evidence: This is an observation from anatomical data supported by citations.

claim: Spanning the EB clockwise starting from tile 1, the fruit fly wedges connect first to the right PB hemisphere, then to the left and so on, while in the locust they connect first to the left, then to the right and so on.
source: Spanning the EB clockwise starting from tile 1, the fruit fly wedges connect first to the right PB hemisphere, then to the left and so on, while in the locust they connect first to the left, then to the right and so on.
evidence: This describes a difference in projection patterns between species.

claim: Despite the difference in projection patterns the effective circuit is preserved between the two species.
source: However, despite this seemingly major difference in projection patterns the effective circuit is preserved between the two species.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis.

claim: The locust P-EN neurons make synapses back to E-PG neurons in the same octant while in the fruit fly they do not.
source: The excitatory portions of the circuits differed in that the locust P-EN neurons make synapses back to E-PG neurons in the same octant while in the fruit fly they do not (Compare Figure 3F with Figure 4F).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The difference in P-EN connectivity resulted from the P-EN synaptic domains being shifted by half-tile in the locust instead of the whole tile shift seen in the fruit fly.
source: This difference resulted from the P-EN synaptic domains being shifted by half-tile in the locust instead of the whole tile shift seen in the fruit fly (Figure 3B and Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The specialisation of the locust together with the cross-innervation of the two medial glomeruli by E-PG neurons enable the closing of the ring in the locust.
source: This specialisation of the locust together with the cross-innervation of the two medial glomeruli by E-PG neurons enable the closing of the ring in the locust.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis.

claim: The E-PG neurons became presynaptically connected to the Delta7 neurons.
source: When we combined the inhibitory and the excitatory sub-circuits into a complete model (Figure 5), the E-PG neurons became presynaptically connected to the Delta7 neurons, in line with (Franconville et al., 2018; Turner-Evans et al., 2019).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5 and supported by citations.

claim: Each Delta7 neuron inhibits the P-EN and P-EG neurons in the same octant, as well as all other Delta7 neurons (for the fruit fly) or a subset (for the locust).
source: Additionally, each Delta7 neuron inhibits the P-EN and P-EG neurons in the same octant, as well as all other Delta7 neurons (for the fruit fly) or a subset (for the locust), as described above.
evidence: This describes the connectivity in the complete model.

claim: The difference in Delta7 connectivity results in two different types of ring attractor topology; one with global inhibition in the fruit fly and another with local inhibition in the locust.
source: This difference results in two different types of ring attractor topology; one with global inhibition in the fruit fly and another with local inhibition in the locust.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis.

claim: Among the excitatory synapses, the P-EN to E-PG and P-EG to E-PG synaptic strengths were the weakest in both species.
source: In both species, among the excitatory synapses, the P-EN to E-PG and P-EG to E-PG synaptic strengths were the weakest
evidence: This is a result from the optimization of synaptic strengths shown in Figure 6.

claim: The synaptic strengths from E-PG to P-EG and P-EN neurons were the strongest in both species.
source: while the synaptic strengths from E-PG to P-EG and P-EN neurons were the strongest.
evidence: This is a result from the optimization of synaptic strengths shown in Figure 6.

claim: The inhibitory synaptic strengths from Delta7 to P-EN and P-EG were stronger in the locust than in the fruit fly.
source: The inhibitory synaptic strengths from Delta7 to P-EN and P-EG were stronger in the locust than in the fruit fly, which was consistent with the fly neurons receiving input from more Delta7 neurons.
evidence: This is a result from the optimization shown in Figure 6.

claim: Both the fruit fly and the locust circuit can operate as ring attractors.
source: Whereas our simulations confirmed that both the fruit fly and the locust circuit can operate as ring attractors
evidence: This is a result from the simulations.

claim: There were clear differences in the spiking activity and dynamics of the two circuits.
source: there were clear differences in the spiking activity and dynamics of the two circuits (Figure 7).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7.

claim: In the locust, there was a strong heading-dependent modulation in the firing of Delta7 neurons, in line with the heading signal location.
source: In the locust, there was a strong heading-dependent modulation in the firing of Delta7 neurons, in line with the heading signal (activity 'bump') location.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: Those Delta7 neurons corresponding to the current heading signal location remained silent in the locust.
source: Those Delta7 neurons corresponding to the current heading signal location remained silent.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations.

claim: In the fruit fly the firing of action potentials was only minimally modulated across the Delta7 population.
source: In contrast, in the fruit fly the firing of action potentials was only minimally modulated across the Delta7 population (Figure 7A and Table 1).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 7 and Table 1.

claim: The difference in Delta7 firing patterns reflected the utilisation of local inhibition in the case of the locust versus the global inhibition in the fruit fly.
source: This difference reflected the utilisation of local inhibition in the case of the locust versus the global inhibition in the fruit fly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: Electrophysiologists have reported pronounced firing rate variation in the locust.
source: Electrophysiologists have indeed reported this pronounced firing rate variation in the locust (Heinze and Homberg, 2007; Heinze et al., 2009; Bockhorst and Homberg, 2015; Pegel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to electrophysiological studies.

claim: In locusts all cell types are consistently tuned more narrowly than in fruit flies (ca. 20%).
source: When comparing the head-direction tuning widths between the two species, we noted that in locusts all cell types are consistently tuned more narrowly (ca. 20%, Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Table 2.

claim: Within both species, the activity 'bump' is wider for E-PG neurons than for the other excitatory neuron classes.
source: Within both species, the activity 'bump' is wider for E-PG neurons than for the other excitatory neuron classes (Table 1)
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Table 1.

claim: The difference in activity 'bump' width is more pronounced in the fruit fly.
source: a difference that is more pronounced in the fruit fly.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Table 1.

claim: The tuning of the Delta7 neurons is the widest across cell types in both species (approx. 96° in the locust).
source: The tuning of the Delta7 neurons is the widest across cell types in both species (approx. 96° in the locust, Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Table 2.

claim: In the fruit fly, the activity is approximately even across all Delta7 neurons (ca. 10% modulation).
source: In the fruit fly, the activity is approximately even across all Delta7 neurons (ca. 10% modulation).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations.

claim: The fruit fly heading signal could jump abruptly from one state to another, whereas the locust circuit exhibited a gradual transition.
source: At a qualitative level, the fruit fly heading signal (the 'bump') could jump abruptly from one state to another, whereas the locust circuit exhibited a gradual transition.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: The results obtained with spiking neuron models were corroborated by rate-based implementations of the models.
source: The results obtained with our spiking neuron models were corroborated by rate-based implementations of the models (Figure 7—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The observed difference in response dynamics is not a consequence of neuron model choice but rather due to the differences in connectivity.
source: confirming that the observed difference in response dynamics is not a consequence of neuron model choice but rather due to the differences in connectivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing spiking and rate-based models.

claim: Changing the global inhibition to local inhibition was sufficient to produce the gradual 'bump' transition observed in the locust circuit.
source: The data generated by this hybrid-species model revealed that changing the global inhibition to local inhibition was sufficient to produce the gradual 'bump' transition we observed in the locust circuit (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a result from the hybrid-species model shown in Figure 8.

claim: The fruit fly ring attractor circuit stabilised to the new heading in approximately half the time it takes for the locust circuit to stabilise, across different magnitudes of angular heading change.
source: The fruit fly ring attractor circuit stabilised to the new heading in approximately half the time it takes for the locust circuit to stabilise, across different magnitudes of angular heading change (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The hybrid-species circuit had a similar response time to the locust circuit.
source: The hybrid-species circuit had a similar response time to the locust circuit.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 8.

claim: The pattern of inhibition in the network is the main contributor to the observed effect on response time.
source: This confirmed that the pattern of inhibition in the network is the main contributor to the observed effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the hybrid-species model results.

claim: The circuit found in the fruit fly is significantly faster than the locust circuit and the hybrid-species circuit with localised inhibition.
source: The resulting angular rate of change values revealed that the circuit found in the fruit fly is significantly faster than the locust circuit and the hybrid-species circuit with localised inhibition (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The transition mode of the heading signal depended on both the extent of the inhibitory synaptic domain width and the angular heading change of the stimulus.
source: Modelling these variations showed that the transition mode of the heading signal depended on both the extent of the inhibitory synaptic domain width and the angular heading change of the stimulus.
evidence: This is a result from varying the inhibition pattern shown in Figure 9.

claim: For both circuits there was a range of low σ values, corresponding to more localised inhibition, which produce gradual transitions ('locust-like').
source: We observed that for both circuits there was a range of low σ values, corresponding to more localised inhibition, which produce gradual transitions ('locust-like').
evidence: This is a result from varying the inhibition pattern shown in Figure 9.

claim: As σ was increased, the inhibitory pattern became more uniform or global, and both circuits transitioned to abrupt jumps ('fly-like').
source: As σ was increased, the inhibitory pattern became more uniform or global, and both circuits transitioned to abrupt jumps ('fly-like').
evidence: This is a result from varying the inhibition pattern shown in Figure 9.

claim: Based on density estimates of dendrites in the PB, the inhibitory synaptic distribution was approximated with a value of σ=0.8 for the locust model, yielding a gradual activity transition regime across the whole range of angular changes.
source: Based on density estimates of dendrites in the PB, we approximated the inhibitory synaptic distribution with a value of σ=0.8 for the locust model, yielding a gradual activity transition regime across the whole range of angular changes.
evidence: This is a modeling choice based on anatomical estimates.

claim: The pattern of inhibition is key to the circuit dynamics in response to rapid heading changes.
source: These results suggested that the pattern of inhibition is indeed key to the circuit dynamics in response to rapid heading changes.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the inhibition pattern variation experiments.

claim: Both the fruit fly and locust circuits had discrete attractor states where the heading signal eventually settled once the stimulus was removed.
source: Both the fruit fly and locust circuits had discrete attractor states where the heading signal eventually settled once the stimulus was removed.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 10.

claim: When a stimulus was applied equidistantly between two attractor states then, once the stimulus was removed, the activity 'bump' moved to one of the two attractor states stochastically due to the presence of noise in the system.
source: When a stimulus was applied equidistantly between two attractor states then, once the stimulus was removed, the activity 'bump' moved to one of the two attractor states stochastically due to the presence of noise in the system (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 10.

claim: The attractor states were more stable and clearly delineated in the locust while in the fruit fly there was a wider distribution of 'bump' locations.
source: These attractor states were more stable and clearly delineated in the locust while in the fruit fly there was a wider distribution of 'bump' locations, indicating that the locust ring attractor is more robust to drift and noise (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 10.

claim: The locust ring attractor is more robust to drift and noise.
source: indicating that the locust ring attractor is more robust to drift and noise (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the attractor state analysis shown in Figure 10.

claim: The ring attractor of the locust was significantly more tolerant to structural noise than the fruit fly circuit.
source: The ring attractor of the locust was significantly more tolerant to structural noise than the fruit fly circuit (Figure 11A).
evidence: This is a result from the noise tolerance experiments shown in Figure 11A.

claim: The reciprocal connections between P-EN and E-PG neurons provide the increased robustness to the locust model.
source: This is exactly what we found (Figure 11A), thus we inferred that these reciprocal connections, between P-EN and E-PG neurons, provide the increased robustness to the locust model.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing the locust and hybrid-species models shown in Figure 11A.

claim: The presence of the P-EG neurons substantially increased the robustness of both species models to the effects of synaptic strength imbalance in the P-EN to E-PG synapses.
source: The presence of the P-EG neurons substantially increased the robustness of both species models to the effects of synaptic strength imbalance in the P-EN to E-PG synapses, as a stable heading signal was observed over a far wider range of synaptic efficacy changes (Figure 11B&C).
evidence: This is a result from the experiments shown in Figure 11B&C.

claim: The P-EG neurons contribute significantly to the tolerance of the ring attractors to synaptic strength asymmetries.
source: The P-EG neurons therefore contribute significantly to the tolerance of the ring attractors to synaptic strength asymmetries.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the P-EG removal experiments.

claim: The locust model was more robust to neuronal heterogeneity than the fruit fly model.
source: Overall, the stability of the ring attractors deteriorated with increased deviation from the nominal values of membrane properties (Figure 12), but the locust model was more robust to these membrane property variations.
evidence: This is a result from the experiments shown in Figure 12.

claim: The distinct heading signal transition regimes (gradual transition in the locust model versus jump in the fruit fly model) were preserved regardless of heterogeneous membrane properties across the neuronal population.
source: Importantly, the distinct heading signal transition regimes (gradual transition in the locust model versus jump in the fruit fly model) were preserved regardless of heterogeneous membrane properties across the neuronal population (Figure 12—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the experiments shown in Figure 12—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both the locust and the fruit fly model reproduced the response dynamics reported by Turner-Evans et al., 2017.
source: Both the locust and the fruit fly model reproduced the response dynamics reported by Turner-Evans et al., 2017.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 13.

claim: The rate by which the heading signal shifts around the ring attractor increases exponentially with increase of uni-hemispheric stimulation strength.
source: Exploration of the response of the circuit to different stimulation strengths showed that the rate by which the heading signal shifts around the ring attractor increases exponentially with increase of uni-hemispheric stimulation strength (Figure 14).
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 14.

claim: The increase in heading signal shift rate was much steeper in the fly.
source: While this general relationship was consistent between the two species, the increase was much steeper in the fly.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 14.

claim: The required stimulus for initiating 'bump' shifting was lower in the fruit fly.
source: Additionally, the required stimulus for initiating 'bump' shifting was lower in the fruit fly.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations shown in Figure 14.

claim: The faster response rate of the fruit fly model to positional stimuli supports their ability to track fast body saccades even when only angular velocity input is available.
source: Both of these aspects concur with the faster response rate of the fruit fly model to positional stimuli and support their ability to track fast body saccades even when only angular velocity input is available.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: Continuous application of angular velocity input caused the heading signal to reach an edge of the PB and then wrap around and continue on the other edge.
source: Continuous application of angular velocity input caused the heading signal to reach an edge of the PB and then wrap around and continue on the other edge.
evidence: This is a result from the simulations.

claim: The wrapping around of the heading signal is present in both models and is thus independent of the physical shape of the EB.
source: This behaviour is present in both models and is thus independent of the physical shape of the EB, that is, whether it forms a closed ring or possesses open ends.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulations.

claim: The wrapping around of the heading signal is supported by the effective closed ring structure found in both species.
source: The wrapping around of the heading signal is required for the animals to track movements that involve turning around its body axis for more that 360° and is supported by the effective closed ring structure we found in both species.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis and simulations.

claim: The faster response of the ring attractor circuit in the fruit fly accommodates the fast body saccades that fruit flies are known to perform.
source: On the one hand, the faster response of the ring attractor circuit in the fruit fly accommodates the fast body saccades that fruit flies are known to perform (Tammero and Dickinson, 2002; Fry et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the modeling results to known behavior, supported by citations.

claim: The locust is a migratory species, so its behaviour demands maintenance of a defined heading for a long period of time.
source: On the other hand, the locust is a migratory species, so its behaviour demands maintenance of a defined heading for a long period of time (Homberg, 2015; de Vries et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to behavioral studies.

claim: The requirement for heading stability might have provided the selective pressure needed to drive the evolution of a more noise resilient head direction circuit in locusts.
source: This requirement for heading stability might have provided the selective pressure needed to drive the evolution of a more noise resilient head direction circuit.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary pressures.

claim: The preservation of the heading tracking circuit across 400 million years of evolutionary divergence suggests that it is an essential, potentially fundamental, part of the insect brain.
source: The preservation of this circuit across 400 million years of evolutionary divergence suggests that it is an essential, potentially fundamental, part of the insect brain.
evidence: This is an inference about the evolutionary significance of the circuit.

claim: In the fruit fly, the torus-shaped EB provides an anatomical solution to the closure of the ring via overlapping projections from E-PG neurons innervating the innermost and outermost PB glomeruli.
source: In the fruit fly, the torus-shaped EB provides an anatomical solution to the closure of the ring via overlapping projections from E-PG neurons innervating the innermost and outermost PB glomeruli.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis.

claim: In the locust the midline spanning output fibers of the E-PG neurons in the medial PB glomeruli serve the function of closing the ring in combination with a slightly different projection pattern that results in the P-EN neurons forming reciprocal connections back to E-PG neurons in the same octant.
source: In contrast, in the locust the midline spanning output fibers of the E-PG neurons in the medial PB glomeruli serve this function in combination with a slightly different projection pattern that results in the P-EN neurons forming reciprocal connections back to E-PG neurons in the same octant.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the circuit analysis.

claim: The large-scale anatomical differences at the level of neuropils and projection patterns do not necessarily affect the core functions of the circuit.
source: In combination, these findings underline that the large-scale anatomical differences at the level of neuropils and projection patterns do not necessarily affect the core functions of the circuit.
evidence: This is a general conclusion from the comparative analysis.

claim: The functional constraints appear significant enough that even in those parts of the circuit that clearly differ between species convergent solutions have evolved that solve similar problems, albeit in slightly different ways.
source: Rather, the functional constraints appear significant enough that even in those parts of the circuit that clearly differ between species convergent solutions have evolved that solve similar problems, albeit in slightly different ways.
evidence: This is a general conclusion about convergent evolution.

claim: The shape of the dendritic arborizations of one type of CX neuron determines how quickly the model circuit tracks rotational movements.
source: First, the shape of the dendritic arborizations of one type of CX neuron determines how quickly the model circuit tracks rotational movements.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling results.

claim: A difference in the overlap of neuronal projections in the EB results in an extra feedback loop between the P-EN and E-PG neurons in the locust circuit that makes it more robust to synaptic noise.
source: Second, a difference in the overlap of neuronal projections in the EB results in an extra feedback loop between the P-EN and E-PG neurons in the locust circuit that makes it more robust to synaptic noise.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling results.
